title: STRENGTH — accept lands on a concrete onboarding next step, tripled-up: inline CTA on the accepted card, welcome-email footer, and a lazily-ensured run so the link works even if the accept-time hook failed

One token serves both legs; a non-accepted token 404s, leaking nothing (onboarding-candidate.ts:17-24).

got: Inline confirm with focus moved to 'Go back' (page.tsx:48-56,290-331); reconcile re-reads authoritative status after a dropped POST (page.tsx:105-118); expired is its own 410 → definite card, not a retry loop (route.ts:32-34, page.tsx:132-135,255-261); markEntryStatus refuses to overwrite terminal/Hired entries and logs the blocked write (offers-store.ts:303-336).

suggested_acceptance: Keep; do not add friction to accept.

title: STRENGTH — offer lifecycle concurrency is production-grade: one open offer per entry (partial unique index + immediate transaction), CAS single-claimer terminal side effects, idempotent re-extends resend the SAME link

suggested_acceptance: Keep; covered by offer-lifecycle.test.ts.

title: STRENGTH — the per-offer deadline lever (commit b7c40a8) is wired end-to-end: Decisions input (1–90d) → mint-time stamp → candidate countdown (coral <48h) → at-most-once T-48h nudge → lazy + swept lapse with audit events
expected: A deadline that actually forces a timely decision and frees headcount.
got: AiReviewCard ttl input (AiReviewCard.tsx:85-100) → route ttlDays (route.ts:50) → validated resolveOfferTtlMs + expires_at at mint (offer-policy.ts:32-36, offers-store.ts:133-135) → page countdown (page.tsx:267-280) → CAS-claimed reminder (offers-store.ts:213-241, offer-reminders.ts:19-46) → expireOfferIfDue on read/respond + heartbeat sweep, both recording offer_expired (offers-store.ts:171-206, instrumentation-node.ts:69-89). l2_priority: Verify the live countdown against a minted short-TTL offer in cs locale (date formatting via Intl, page.tsx:272-274).

title: STRENGTH — the pre-boarding questionnaire is a visible, nudged loop (commit 3c9f4f8): pending/done chip on every run card, answers pre-fill the run detail, submission stamps the timeline, and one deliverability-checked nudge fires on the heartbeat

l2_priority: Submit the questionnaire as the candidate and verify the chip + answers on the Onboarding tab.

title: STRENGTH — Hired is protected as an outcome-bearing terminal: a manual stage move to Hired is 422-refused and routed through the offer flow, so every hire has an offer record, an acceptance, and an onboarding hand-off
expected: No 'hire' can exist without its decision trail.
got: set_stage → Hired returns 422 with an instructive message (route.ts:96-107); the only path to Hired is the candidate's accept (offer-finalize.ts:57-66), which also seals the outcome + fires onboarding + mirrors to a configured ATS (offer-finalize.ts:79-129).
ceiling: A genuinely out-of-band hire (walk-in, referral signed on paper) has no expressible path except minting a pro-forma offer and accepting it on the candidate's behalf.
suggested_acceptance: Keep; verify the 422 message guides the recruiter to 'move to Offer → extend'.

title: Command-bar 'advance top N' bare-advances an Offer-stage candidate to Hired — no offer, no comms, no onboarding; a drafted offer is silently discarded
expected: Hired is terminal and outcome-bearing: reached only when the candidate accepts an extended offer. The manual set_stage path enforces exactly this (422 + guidance), and the accept route special-cases offer_review into extendOffer. Every advance path should share that invariant.
got: The command bar's execute path calls actOnPipelineEntry(e.id, 'accept', ...) directly (app/api/pipeline/command/route.ts:101-102), skipping the route-level offer logic (app/api/pipeline/[id]/route.ts:226-228). affected() only excludes stage==='Hired' (command/route.ts:28-34), so an Offer-stage candidate in the top N falls into the generic accept branch (app/_lib/db/pipeline.ts:1332-1341): stage Offer→Hired, approval_kind (a drafted offer_review payload) cleared, 'advanced' event recorded. No offer record, no dispatchOffer, no onboarding — the exact bypass the set_stage guard (app/api/pipeline/[id]/route.ts:97-107) exists to prevent. Top-scored candidates are precisely the ones likely to be at Offer, and the preview shows their stage but not this consequence.
l2_priority: Run 'advance top 5' live with an Offer-stage candidate in the top 5 (seed has 4 at Offer). Confirm: entry lands Hired with no offers row, the drafted offer_review payload is gone, and no offer/onboarding comm exists in the Outbox.
suggested_acceptance: advance_top either excludes Offer-stage entries (with the preview saying why), or routes an Offer-stage/offer_review entry through the same extendOffer path the accept route uses — Hired is never reachable without an offer record.

title: Candidate-notifying bulk actions preview WHO but never WHAT — no rendered-letter dry-run on bulk reject, command-bar reject, or the pass preview
expected: Marek's scored criterion: each bulk action offers a dry-run showing who it touches AND the rendered message each person will receive, before committing (absent = major).
got: Board bulk reject: two-step confirm with a count only (PipelineTab.tsx:1013-1044). Command-bar reject: preview rows are {label, score, jobTitle, stage} (CommandBar.tsx:96-106, command/route.ts:12,37-43) plus the honest 'Reject and notify' description — still no letter. PassPreviewModal lists decisions + reasons, not letters (PassPreviewModal.tsx:37-45). The rejection template is deterministic and locale-resolved (comms-dispatch.ts:194-205), so rendering it in the preview is structurally cheap — the data exists, the UI never shows it.
l2_priority: Bulk-reject 2 candidates live: record exactly what the confirm step shows, then open the resulting letters (drawer comms + Outbox) and check what Marek could NOT have reviewed beforehand (language, personalization, merge fields).
suggested_acceptance: Every candidate-notifying bulk commit gate can expand at least one rendered sample letter (per locale/archetype variant) before confirm; the command-bar reject preview links the template it will send.

title: LLM-authored candidate-facing bodies (outreach draft, offer letter) receive no locale signal — a Czech candidate can get a mixed-language letter under the bank's name
expected: All candidate-facing messages render correctly in the candidate's language (Marek's scored criterion; SIM3 established entry.locale as the source of truth).
got: Only the 'prep' task passes --lang to the Python prompt (app/_lib/automation-run.ts:171-172, cache axis :137-138); outreach/rejection/offer prompts get no locale. comms-dispatch.ts:18-24 documents the seam: 'The LLM-authored bodies (outreach, the offer letter) stay as the model produced them — only their deterministic chrome localizes.' dispatchOffer then appends a locale-pinned footer to whatever language the letter came back in (comms-dispatch.ts:241-243). Deterministic templates (rejection, invites, confirmations) ARE correctly locale-resolved (comms-dispatch.ts:39-47) — the gap is exactly the two highest-stakes letters.
l2_priority: Generate an outreach draft and an offer draft for a cs-locale candidate; assert the body language (the model may or may not infer Czech from the CV — code guarantees nothing).
suggested_acceptance: The outreach and offer prompts receive the entry's locale (same --lang plumbing prep already has, added as a cache axis), and the drafted letter's language matches entry.locale.

title: Drag/select to Hired always fails with a generic — and misleading — message; the server's actionable 422 guidance is discarded by both clients
expected: The Hired guard is correct by design; when it refuses, the recruiter should see the server's own explanation: 'Hired is set when the candidate accepts an offer... Move them to Offer and extend an offer.'
got: The Hired column is a live drop target (PipelineBoard.tsx:77-94,300-305) and the drawer's move select lists Hired (CandidateDrawer.tsx:704). On the 422, the board shows t('moveFailed') — cs: 'Kandidáta se nepodařilo přesunout — tabule byla obnovena', which wrongly implies a concurrent change (PipelineTab.tsx:554-562); the drawer catch also drops data.error for its own generic string (CandidateDrawer.tsx:276-284). The one message that teaches the correct offer-flow grammar (app/api/pipeline/[id]/route.ts:102-107) never reaches the user. Recurs on every attempted hire-by-drag until the grammar is learned elsewhere.
l2_priority: Drag a card onto the Hired column live; capture the message shown vs the 422 body. Also check whether a recruiter can discover the Offer→extend path from the board alone.
suggested_acceptance: A refused move surfaces the server's specific reason (at minimum for the 422 Hired case), distinct from the 409 concurrent-change message; ideally the Hired column drop target signals 'via offer only' before the drop.

title: The internal board's activity feed shows initials only — the public anonymizing projection is applied to the operator's own workspace
expected: The recruiter on their own board can tell WHICH candidate an event concerns ('M. K. advanced · Teller' is ambiguous at 50-200 candidates).
got: GET /api/pipeline/events (no ?entry=) always serves the public projection — initials, no entry id (app/api/pipeline/events/route.ts:42-46; app/_lib/pipeline-events-public.ts:34-54) — because the route is unauthenticated and the reduction is a deliberate PII fix (pipeline-events-public.ts:3-18, 'when an auth layer lands... the full feed can return'). The board feed renders that projection (PipelineTab.tsx:1150-1156) and event rows aren't clickable through to a candidate. The per-entry drawer history keeps full fidelity (events/route.ts:24-30).
scope_note: The anonymization itself is a security strength (documented no-auth mitigation), not the defect; the cost it externalizes onto the internal operator is. Resolves properly only with the planned auth layer.
l2_priority: Confirm live that feed rows are initials-only and non-navigable; measure how a recruiter resolves 'who was that?' (search by initials fails).
suggested_acceptance: Once auth lands, authenticated recruiters get full names + click-through on the feed; until then, feed rows at least deep-link to a board search that can resolve the initials.

title: An expired offer renders as 'offer extended' (twice) in the drawer timeline — the lapse event the data layer deliberately emits is mislabeled by the renderer
expected: candidate-timeline.ts pushes {kind:'offer', status:'expired', at: expiresAt} precisely 'so it doesn't render as extended forever' — the drawer should show the lapse.
got: TimelineItemRow maps offer statuses accepted/declined and defaults EVERYTHING else to t('offerExtended') (CandidateDrawer.tsx:938-940), and messages/cs.json pipeline.drawer.timeline has no offerExpired key — so an expired offer shows two 'extended' rows (mint + deadline), reading like a re-extend instead of a lapse. Contradicts the journey's 'no silent state loss' bar for the money path.
l2_priority: Expire an offer (short ttlDays) and open the drawer: confirm the double 'extended' rendering.
suggested_acceptance: status 'expired' renders its own label ('Nabídka propadla' + deadline); unknown future statuses fall back to the raw status, never to 'extended'.

title: NL command bar is English-only inside the Czech workspace — grammar matches English verbs and the server echoes hardcoded English descriptions
expected: The journey language is cs; both characters work the Czech UI all day. A Czech recruiter should be able to type 'zamítni pod 60 %' — or at least read the preview description in Czech.
got: parseCommand matches only English patterns (reject...below / advance...top / run policy — app/_lib/pipeline-command.ts:41-55); describeCommand returns hardcoded English strings (:62-79) rendered verbatim in the preview (CommandBar.tsx:91,93), while all surrounding chrome IS Czech (messages/cs.json pipeline.command). Result: a mixed-language surface requiring English incantations. The board/drawer catalogs are otherwise fully Czech.
l2_priority: Type a Czech command ('zamítni pod 60') live — confirm it lands as 'unknown' with an English 'Didn't catch that.'
suggested_acceptance: Czech verb aliases in the parser + describeCommand keyed through the i18n catalog (or the documented LLM fallback for free-form phrasing, which would also cover cs).

title: No undo/recall affordance where the batch fires — reinstate exists, but per-candidate and on the Decisions tab only
expected: Marek's criterion: bulk/irreversible actions offer an undo or recall path. After a misfired bulk reject he wants a one-click 'reinstate these N' where the result message appears.
got: A guarded, sealed per-candidate reinstate action exists (app/api/pipeline/[id]/route.ts:166-189) and is surfaced in DecisionsTab (app/features/sub_decisions/DecisionsTab.tsx), but the board's bulk-result line ('rejected N · failed M', PipelineTab.tsx:972-990) offers no path back; rejected entries also vanish from the board immediately (listPipeline excludes terminal statuses, app/_lib/db/pipeline.ts:286-306), so the batch's subjects aren't even visible to re-select. The letters themselves are unrecallable (inherent to comms), which makes the pre-send preview (pa-no-rendered-message-preview) the real control.
l2_priority: After a live bulk reject, measure the actual path to reverse one candidate (board → Decisions → find → reinstate): steps + whether Marek would find it unaided.
suggested_acceptance: The bulk-reject result line links 'Reinstatovat' / opens the rejected cohort in Decisions pre-filtered to the batch.

title: Ship-bar note: candidate comms triggered from the board are outbox-simulated by default — 'queued' is a terminal dev state, and recipients are names, not addresses
expected: For the 'public product path' ship bar: advancing/rejecting that claims to notify a candidate actually reaches an inbox.
got: sendComm routes to a durable local Outbox unless COMMS_WEBHOOK_URL is set (app/_lib/comms.ts:97-100); 'queued' is documented as terminal-in-dev — nothing dequeues it (comms.ts:12-17,34-42). Even with a relay, the recipient contract resolves to a display name / candidate id, never an email, except inbound applicants who supplied contact (comms.ts:19-23; comms-dispatch.ts:49-68) — so seeded/Match-sourced candidates dead-letter at any real relay. The system is honest about all of this (statuses, dead-letter alerts, docs/COMMS_DELIVERY.md), so this is a named seam, not a hidden one.
ceiling: Until a relay (COMMS_WEBHOOK_URL) plus a name→address directory (or captured contact) exist, no board-triggered rejection/invite/offer reaches a real inbox — the Outbox row is the delivery. The UI's 'sent/queued/failed' language stays honest about it.
scope_note: Demo-disclaimed in code + docs; severity dropped one level per rubric. Kept visible (not accepted-gaps) because it gates the run's 'public product path' ship bar.
l2_priority: Verify the drawer/Outbox render 'queued' (channel 'outbox') for a board-triggered rejection, and that no UI copy overclaims delivery.

title: Strength: every stage move is CAS-guarded end to end — optimistic drag with rollback + visible alert, per-item expectedStage in bulk, IMMEDIATE transactions in the DB
expected: The journey DoD: 'the move sticks (no silent revert)' and no stale view clobbers a concurrent change.
got: Drag sends the card's own prior stage as expectedStage and rolls back WITH a dismissible alert on failure (PipelineTab.tsx:544-565); bulk move/decide carry per-card expectedStage and keep failures selected for retry (PipelineTab.tsx:447-504); the route answers a CAS miss with 409 + the fresh entry (app/api/pipeline/[id]/route.ts:108-123); the DB read-compute-write runs in an IMMEDIATE transaction (app/_lib/db/pipeline.ts:1232-1257,1394-1433). Do not touch this grammar.

title: Strength: the drawer's unified timeline is real — pipeline events + analyses + interview + invites + offers merged chronologically, with full comms letters (including failed sends) in their own section
expected: The journey's central check: a drawer that shows the WHOLE story, not stage changes only.
got: candidateTimeline joins analyses (exact-label join, honestly scoped), interview created/completed, invites sent/confirmed (slot shown), offers extended/answered/expired (app/_lib/candidate-timeline.ts:38-85); the drawer merges it with per-entry events into one time-ordered list (CandidateDrawer.tsx:208-218,665-689), analysis rows deep-link to the saved report with the recruiter's disposition chip (:926-969), and the comms section shows the actual letters with failed sends visually flagged (:636-663).
l2_priority: Spot-check on live data that an analysis AND a schedule invite both appear for one candidate (the exact-label analysis join is the fragile edge).

title: Strength: consistent preview-then-confirm grammar on every mutating gate, with honest 'and notify' disclosure and per-candidate comms-failure isolation
expected: Marek's world: nothing bulk fires blind.
got: Command bar previews the affected set and executes only with confirm:true, mapping to the SAME guarded actions (no new privilege — command/route.ts:44-66); its reject path queues a rejection comm per candidate with isolation + a 'rejection_comms_failed' audit event when one fails (command/route.ts:86-99); the copy discloses 'Reject and notify' (pipeline-command.ts:66-70); the policy pass gets a dry-run modal that renders rejects first and surfaces fairness-blocked holds separately (PassPreviewModal.tsx:15-45); bulk reject is two-step confirmed (PipelineTab.tsx:1013-1044). Human accept/reject/reinstate are sealed into the tamper-evident decision chain ([id]/route.ts:249-260).

title: One-click manual Reject on a queue card: no confirmation, silent candidate email, no undo
expected: Rejecting a candidate from an AI review card — an irreversible, candidate-facing action — asks for confirmation (or previews the rendered rejection message), confirms the send afterward, and offers a way back.
got: AiReviewCard's Reject is a single click; the card animates out optimistically and the API unconditionally dispatches the rejection email (route.ts:262) with no confirmation of the send. The reconsider/undo queue joins only `auto_rejected` events, so a manually rejected candidate never appears in it (documented as deliberate).
suggested_acceptance: A queue-card Reject shows a confirm step naming the candidate and the message that will be sent; after the send, an explicit confirmation states what went to whom; a mis-clicked manual reject has a recall/reinstate path (or the reconsider queue includes recent human rejects).
l2_priority: Reject one candidate from a screening card live: verify the email lands in the Channels outbox with no UI confirmation, and that the candidate is absent from the reconsider queue.
scope_note: Sending mechanics are comms-scope; this finding is about the decision affordance (confirm/undo/feedback), which is Decisions-scope.

title: Null match score coerces to 0 — an unscored candidate is auto-rejectable on a fabricated number
expected: A candidate with no match score (never scored / degraded intake) is excluded from the auto-reject wave or flagged 'unscored' for manual review; a sealed adverse record never asserts a measurement that was not taken.
got: runScreenWave sorts and thresholds on `matchScore ?? 0` with no null exclusion in the cohort filter — a never-scored candidate ranks worst, passes `0 < maxMatchToReject`, and (unless fairness-protected by archetype) is auto-rejected with a sealed rationale claiming 'match 0 < 45'. The preview shows them as 'match 0', indistinguishable from a genuine zero, so the human gate cannot reliably catch it.
suggested_acceptance: An entry with matchScore=null at Screened is either excluded from the wave cohort (listed separately as 'unscored — needs review') or visibly marked unscored in the preview; a sealed record never renders a null score as 0.
l2_priority: Seed a Screened entry with matchScore=null (e.g. degraded intake), open the wave: confirm whether it appears as 'match 0' in the would-reject list and what the sealed record says after commit.

title: Auto-rejection email has no automated-decision disclosure and no contest / human-review channel
expected: A candidate adversely affected by automated processing is told automation was involved and offered a route to request human intervention / contest the decision (GDPR Art. 22(3), AI Act transparency).
got: dispatchRejection sends the same template for auto and manual rejects; the copy reads 'After careful review, we won't be moving forward' — implying individual human review of an automated threshold decision — with no automation disclosure and no contest affordance. The GDPR footer covers data access/erasure only. The reconsider path exists but is recruiter-initiated and invisible to the subject.
suggested_acceptance: The rejection comm for an auto-rejected candidate (dispatchRejection with automated:true) includes a plain-language sentence disclosing automated processing with human approval, plus a reply/link channel to request human re-review; the manual-reject template stays as-is.
l2_priority: Commit a small wave and read the actual outbox message body for an auto-rejected candidate — confirm the absence of disclosure/contest language in both locales.
scope_note: Comms delivery/channels are out of journey scope; this is the content of the decision notice, judged under Lucie's disclosure lens.

title: Sealed record of a human decision omits the AI recommendation it ratified
expected: When a recruiter accepts/rejects from an AI screening card, the sealed decision record captures what the AI recommended (verdict, confidence, rationale, model/source) so a right-to-explanation dossier shows both the machine input and the human call.
got: The human accept/reject seal writes only { fromStage, detail } as inputs with a default rationale like 'Recruiter accept from Screened'. The AI recommendation lives in mutable approval_detail (set by automation-run) and is cleared on decision — the chain cannot reproduce what the human saw. Model/version is captured nowhere in the record.
suggested_acceptance: For an accept/reject on an entry carrying a *_review approval, the sealed inputs include the approval payload snapshot (recommendation, confidence, source) and the payload's model/source field; the dossier for that candidate shows the AI input alongside the human decision.
l2_priority: Accept one AI screening card live, then export the decision dossier for that candidate and confirm the AI recommendation is absent from the sealed record.

title: approvedBy in the immutable record is unauthenticated free text, defaulting to a generic constant
expected: The 'who approved this reviewed set' claim in a sealed Art. 22 record names an authenticated person.
got: The route accepts any `approvedBy` string from the request body with no identity check; absent one, operatorApprover() writes 'operator (single-operator deployment)' (or KP_OPERATOR_NAME if set). The code documents this seam honestly — but the central attribution claim is either generic or client-suppliable.
ceiling: Single-operator deployment with no per-user identity: a truly authenticated approver name requires the multi-user auth layer; until then KP_OPERATOR_NAME is a deployment precondition, and the client-supplied approvedBy should be dropped or bound to the session.
suggested_acceptance: The commit path derives approvedBy from the server-side session/env only (never the request body); deployments without KP_OPERATOR_NAME get a startup/UI warning on the records panel.
l2_priority: Commit a wave, export the dossier: confirm what approvedBy actually reads in the sealed record on this deployment.

title: Role row shows pending-decision chips but the wave acts on the whole Screened cohort — counts differ, scope unexplained
expected: The wave modal states whose cohort it operates on, and the discrepancy with the row that launched it (N chips vs M cohort) is self-explanatory.
got: RoleDecisionRow renders entries with approvalKind='decision' (the pending queue slice); runScreenWave's cohort is ALL active entries at stage 'Screened' for the jobId. The modal shows the server cohort count but never explains the scope, so the recruiter may believe the wave targets the chips they just saw.
suggested_acceptance: The wave modal's subtitle names the cohort ('all N candidates at Screened for this role'), so a count differing from the row is explained before the preview renders.
l2_priority: With a role whose pending-chip count differs from its Screened cohort, open the wave and check whether the mismatch is noticeable/confusing live.

title: Reinstate restores the pipeline but offers no candidate follow-up, though the rejection email already went out

title: Strength: preview-first wave with a server-enforced human-approval token (Art. 22 gate is structural, not copy)
got: Dry-run on open + every slider change with zero mutation; commit requires the SHA-256 approval token of the exact previewed reject set, recomputed server-side from the live cohort; missing/stale token → 409 → forced re-preview; the commit loop reads from the same signed set so committed ≠ reviewed is impossible.
suggested_acceptance: Protect: do not weaken the token gate for convenience (e.g. auto-retry commit after 409).

title: Strength: fairness gate is server-side and fail-closed; tie-break never splits equal scores, resolved in the candidate's favour
got: Early-career AND unknown/renamed archetypes are shielded from auto-rejection at the decision point (not just in UI copy); unknown archetypes write a drift marker on commit; the tie-safe cutoff keeps a straddling tied run whole (kept, not rejected); small cohorts get a documented min-1 policy so an enabled rule can't silently no-op.
suggested_acceptance: Protect: keep the gate at the decision point; never move shielding into client-side filtering.

title: Strength: tamper-evident decision chain covering the auto-reject, the human decision, AND the reversal, with verify + one-click export

ceiling: Records are best-effort (sealDecisionSafe never throws) — a seal failure logs and proceeds, so the chain is near-complete, not guaranteed-complete; and human-decision records are thin (SD-L1-004).

title: Strength: screening override validated + clamped at the route AND re-validated at the destructive operation
got: A malformed/out-of-range override is a 400 at the boundary, and runScreenWave re-validates before merging into the live config — a raw {rejectBottomPercent:9999} can never reach the bottom-% math through any caller; only clamped known fields merge.

title: Strength: reconsider queue makes the auto-reject undo real — guarded, audited, and sealed

title: Strength: localized rationales render from a structured mirror while the sealed English string stays byte-stable

Recipient for sourced/rediscovered candidates resolves to a human NAME (never an email — 'the data model stores none'), which the contract says a relay 'cannot deliver to … will dead-letter'. title: The rediscovery WHY-NOW is a per-kind stock template (3 fixed sentences), not this candidate's fit-delta story

It IS grounded in the real prior outcome and the real deterministic score (better than a bare name), but the candidate-specific delta (matchedSkills / missing skills are present in the ranked payload rows) is dropped before the why-now is rendered — a dressed-up re-score.
l2_priority: Run rediscovery on a role with ≥3 silver medalists and read the rows side by side: do the why-now lines visibly repeat the same 3 sentences?
suggested_acceptance: Why-now composed from the candidate's ranked-row detail (top matched skills for THIS role, the requirement that sank them last time if derivable) rather than a kind-keyed template.

title: Reach out fails with 404 'job not found' for any in-app-created role — the outreach draft resolves the job from the static seed corpus, not the DB
expected: The outreach draft uses the authoritative server-side job record (the journey file assumes route.ts:43-51's trust posture extends to the draft).

In-app ingested/published roles exist only in SQLite (jobs table) → Reach out 404s on them; an in-app-EDITED seed role drafts from stale seed facts. The TS comment 'Other tasks score a single job and skip the corpus entirely' is wrong — they resolve the job FROM the corpus (the same gap idea-e01935e9 fixed for rematch only).
l2_priority: Ingest + publish a fresh role in-app, open its candidates/rediscover tab, click Reach out → expect the 404 'job not found' error surfaced on the button.
suggested_acceptance: Outreach (and screen/rejection/prep/scorecard/offer) receive the live DB job via --job-json, mirroring rankPoolForJob and the campaign route.

title: Analysis-sourced pool candidates can be ranked and rediscovered but NOT reached out — 400 'candidate profile not found', and the failed attempt still silently files them into the pipeline
expected: Any candidate the pool ranks and rediscovery surfaces can be outreached; a failed outreach leaves no half-handled state.

Result: AutomationError 400. Compounding: createPipelineEntry runs BEFORE the draft, so the errored candidate is filed at Screened anyway — which removes them from the rediscover list on next load (hist jobId===job.id && active filter), leaving them looking 'handled' with no first touch sent.
l2_priority: Reach out on an analysis-sourced rediscovered candidate → expect the 400 error on the row AND the candidate appearing on the pipeline board at Screened with no outreach_sent event.
suggested_acceptance: runAutomationTask falls back to the analysis payload (poolEntryFromAnalysis path) when no profile row exists, or the outreach route resolves via resolveCandidatePoolEntry before filing the entry.

On the current seed fixture the caps likely aren't hit (frequency low today) — at ČS scale (thousands of past applicants) the core promise silently breaks, with zero UI signal.
l2_priority: Optional: seed >100 profiles and confirm the rediscover panel gives no truncation hint.
suggested_acceptance: When a cap is hit, the /rediscover and /candidates payloads carry a truncation flag the panels render (mirroring the existing 'more' count pattern in rediscover.ts:97-102).

title: The interviewer's full internal brief — including submission-debrief red flags marked 'never say this aloud' — is returned to the candidate's browser by /connect, and ElevenLabs grounding rides on a client-side, tamperable prompt override

For OpenAI the instructions are already delivered server-side at credential mint (openai.ts:92-109) — returning them to the browser is pure exposure; for ElevenLabs the brief is pushed as a client-side agent-prompt override (VoiceInterview.tsx:545-549), which also means the client controls what prompt the agent actually runs (an overrides-enabled agent accepts whatever the browser sends on the signed URL).

title: The review surface is evidence-anchored end to end: scorecard quotes click-jump to the exact transcript turn, human and AI scorecards are visually distinct, failed calls are never scored, and the verdict is sealed with its model version
expected: A transcript + usable result she can defend to a manager — not raw audio to re-listen.
got: findEvidenceTurn anchors each rating's quote to a transcript turn with a distinctive-word majority guard so paraphrases aren't mis-anchored (InterviewTranscriptModal.tsx:46-68); anchored quotes are clickable jump-to-moment buttons and cited turns are badged (:216-244, :263). The human scorecard renders coral-tinted so the two are never confused (:110-132). Upstream honesty: only a live, ≥1-turn, error-free call is 'completed' (finalize-status.ts:34-37); a failed call's transcript is never scored and never sets the Interview→Offer approval (complete/route.ts:150-159); the transcript persists BEFORE scoring so no phantom gate approval can exist (:118-134); transcript truncation is logged, not silent (interview-run.ts:258-265); the AI verdict is sealed as a decision record with the scorecard prompt version as actor (:168-179).

l2_priority: On a real completed session, click 2-3 evidence quotes and confirm each lands on the correct turn; check one deliberately paraphrased quote renders unanchored, not wrongly anchored.
suggested_acceptance: Every rating with evidence either jumps to its true source turn or renders as plain text — never to an unrelated turn.

The meter gate books the whole call, not one leftover minute (create/route.ts:30-31); minutes debit idempotently on the applied completion only (complete/route.ts:143-148).

suggested_acceptance: At any moment at most one usable link exists per entry, and no recruiter action can kill a call that is actually in progress without an explicit override.

title: Every lifecycle state she can meet renders an honest card — completed, revoked, expired — the shown duration is the session's real run-of-show length, and a dropped call keeps her link retryable instead of locking her out
expected: An honest 'completed / a human reviews this' close, never a dead Start button; the stated length is the real one.
got: Completed → closed thank-you card (page.tsx:26-33, cs.json:761-762); revoked/expired → honest inactive card (page.tsx:39-46) using the single expiry authority shared with the credential gate (db/interviews.ts:203-212) so page and API can never disagree. Duration comes from session.durationMin with a documented grounded default (page.tsx:24, :58; interview-duration.mjs:25-44 — the provider cap clears the grounded maximum so a real 20-30 min interview is never severed). In-client, a completed ending swaps controls for the same closing card the server renders (VoiceInterview.tsx:674-681) while a failed ending (zero-turn, error blip, never-live) keeps retry (finalize-status.ts:34-37; VoiceInterview.tsx:102-108); her answers survive a tab close via sendBeacon persisted as 'failed', never scored (VoiceInterview.tsx:372-387; complete/route.ts:150-159), and a save failure is told to her (VoiceInterview.tsx:278-281, cs.json:794).

suggested_acceptance: No state of /interview/[token] ever shows a Start button that cannot work, and the stated duration equals the session's stored run-of-show length.

title: AI disclosure + consent clear her bar: plain-Czech, unticked, refusable, enforced server-side at both credential-mint and transcript-persist, with a truthful 'human decides' claim and a jurisdiction-aware disclosure
